title: Documentation support (MEAT) for chronic conditions
question: Which chronic condition, if any, is supported for risk adjustment by this note? Ignore the reason for the visit. Choose 'no code' if none is supported.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for persistent lower back pain.

HPI
The patient is a 62-year-old male presenting for evaluation of chronic low back pain that has persisted for the last three months. He describes the pain as a dull ache localized to the lumbar region, which worsens with prolonged sitting or heavy lifting. He denies any radiating pain, numbness, or weakness in the lower extremities. He reports that over-the-counter ibuprofen provides minimal relief. He denies any recent falls or acute trauma to the spine.

Medication List
Ibuprofen 400mg as needed; Lisinopril 10mg daily.

Exam
Patient is alert and oriented. He appears in no acute distress. Spine is visualized; there is mild tenderness to palpation over the L4-L5 paraspinal muscles. Range of motion is limited by discomfort but remains within functional limits. Neurological exam of the lower extremities is intact with normal strength and sensation.

Assessment
1. Chronic low back pain.

Plan
1. Physical therapy: Referred to outpatient PT for lumbar strengthening and stretching exercises.
2. Activity modification: Advised to avoid heavy lifting for the next two weeks.
3. Follow-up: Return to clinic in four weeks to assess progress with physical therapy.

Problem List
1. chronic systolic heart failure (HFrEF)
2. Chronic low back pain
explanations: Heart failure appears only in a problem list and is not addressed in this encounter, so it is not supported for this date of service.

distractors.why: A problem-list entry alone does not show the condition affected care at this visit.
